$comment: Every gate in this repository is supposed to have been proven capable of failing, by a
mutation that COMPILES — a non-compiling mutation is a false red and proves nothing. That
practice was manual and unrecorded, so the proof existed in a reviewer's memory and expired
with it. This register is the practice written down and executed.
It replaces a Stryker job that could not produce a score. Under xUnit v3 every test project
builds as its own executable; dotnet-stryker 4.16.0 with the VsTest runner injects mutants
and never activates them, so all 153 tests pass and the score is 0.00 %, and with the
dotnettest runner it exits 1 after startup with no diagnostic. A tool that cannot measure
is worse than no tool, because its number is read as one.
What this register measures is narrower and true: for each entry, the named tests fail when
the patch is applied and pass when it is not. That is a kill, demonstrated, on the gates that
carry the architecture rules — not a percentage over every mutable line.

mutations.why: Makes the manifest writer emit no policies array. Six flows across five samples attach a policy, so the document would tell every reader those flows run unpoliced.
Puts a per-flow topic into a transport's configuration. The address and the flow it belongs to become two facts in two places, and renaming the flow no longer renames the address.
Adds an emitter that no trigger kind accounts for — a derived surface nobody has decided the rules for.
Suppresses producedBy for any event with a single producer. A reader then cannot tell an event nothing emits from one the compiler did not look at, which is the failure ADR-0017 F1 catalogues.

Adds a field to the published schema that nothing writes. Absence of that field then reads to every consumer as 'this application has none' rather than 'nobody looked' — the promise the schema's additionalProperties: false makes, broken in the direction nobody notices.

Adds a fitness function without updating the count the paper quotes. The paper is a second declaration of facts the tree already holds, and this is that second declaration going stale — the exact failure the paper is about, applied to itself.

Moves the route on a flow that carries two triggers, so its second address is no longer where the flow declares it. Deleting the attribute outright was tried first and is a FALSE RED: it is the assembly's only [HttpTrigger], so FlowXEndpoints.g.cs is not generated at all and the host stops compiling — a mutation that does not build proves nothing about the tests.

Makes the generated starter run the plan on the raw delivery instead of on what the decoder produced. FLOWX1051 lets a flow keep its own input contract because a decoder bridges the gap; if the emitter drops that, the relaxation is paid for at run time by a first step that finds nothing under the key it binds.
